page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Identify f(x) and f′(x)
steps.why: Differentiating log(secx) by the chain rule — (1/secx) times the derivative of secx — gives exactly tanx, confirming f(x)=log secx and f′(x)=tanx.
common_mistakes: Taking f(x)=tanx instead, which would need f′(x)=sec²x, not log secx — the bracket does not match that pairing.
Losing the chain-rule factor of 1/secx when differentiating log secx.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiate the LOG term to check: d/dx[log secx] = tanx exactly — that confirms which term is f(x).

steps.label: Apply the formula for the final answer

lines.text: ∴ ∫ eˣ(tanx + log secx) dx = eˣ log secx + c

steps.why: Substituting f(x)=log secx into the standard formula gives the final answer directly, keeping only the logarithmic term multiplied by eˣ.
common_mistakes: Writing eˣ tanx as the final answer instead of eˣ log secx.
steps.memory_tip: The answer keeps the LOG term (f(x)), not the simpler tanx term — easy to swap by instinct, but wrong.
